unmapped_findings: Peak (flow) stress of this sample at 1100 °C and 0.01 s^-1 is approximately 65 MPa, read from Fig. 3(b) (true stress–true strain curves at T = 1100 °C for four strain rates).

The dynamic recrystallization activation energy of the steel computed by the Arrhenius hyperbolic-sine method is 669.844 kJ mol^-1 (average value within the experimental range 900–1150 °C, 0.01–10 s^-1), based on average slopes k1 = 5.135 and k2 = 15.690.
The Zener-Hollomon parameter lnZ for this sample (1100 °C, 0.01 s^-1) is 54.08 (Table 1).

No condition-specific DRX average grain size value is reported in the text for 1100 °C / 0.01 s^-1; only a curve (Fig. 10 / Fig. 11a) is given, from which the 0.01 s^-1 series reaches just below 80 µm at 1150 °C (grain size exceeds 70 µm).

The DRX average grain size prediction model for the steel is d_rex = 807743.63·ε̇^(-0.1903)·exp(-120648.47/RT) + 4.338, with R = 0.996 and MRE = 4.53% for all samples (global, not condition-specific).

The sample corresponds to Fig. 9(a) (T = 1100 °C, ε̇ = 0.01 s^-1); the paper states that at 1100 °C with decreasing strain rate the recrystallized grains grow and microstructure heterogeneity improves.
The material composition is Fe-25.14Mn-10Al-1.46C-0.053Nb (mass fraction %), rest Fe; same steel batch/composition used to confirm reproducibility under identical experimental conditions.
